basis: Umbrella of gonadal differentiation and androgen synthesis/action disorders; renal and other organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Substance dependence has no organ axis; associated risks do not establish direct organ damage.
Digital malformations, microcephaly and gastrointestinal atresias are defining features; intellectual disability occurs in 39/77. Cardiac, renal and hearing defects are uncommon.
Neoplasm located in the parietal lobe of the brain.
Inherited retinal degeneration with photoreceptor dysfunction and visual loss.
Benign vascular neoplasm arising in the brain or meninges; both intracranial location and blood-vessel origin define it.
Supplied definition and developmental-disorder ancestry include fetal cognitive injury; specific cardiac, skeletal and renal malformations vary across the group.
Human trichostrongyloid infections predominantly involve intestinal nematodes; pulmonary involvement is not characteristic across the group.
Plasmalogen synthesis defect with rhizomelia and cataracts; severe neurodevelopmental impairment is typical, reported in 1/1; cardiac and palatal findings omitted at the cap.
No common mapped organ of origin: usual mediastinal and retroperitoneal germ-cell sites lack an axis; CNS and gastrointestinal origins are site-specific subtypes.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy centered in the pancreas; pancreatic location and lymphoma mechanisms define the disease.
HbS/Lepore hemoglobinopathy causes sickling and hemolytic anemia; additional organ damage is not established as common in this rare subtype.
Callosal agenesis, intellectual disability and digital skeletal anomalies define it; cardiac defects occur in 5/22; pinna dysmorphism alone does not establish hearing damage.
Hydrocephalus, endocardial fibroelastosis and cataracts define the syndrome; respiratory insufficiency does not establish direct pulmonary injury.
Ketolysis/isoleucine metabolic defect causes episodic ketoacidosis; altered consciousness is usually transient and persistent neurologic injury is a minority feature.
Defined by neurodevelopmental, endocrine and exocrine pancreatic disease; cholestatic liver injury 7/7; hearing loss 7/7 and reported retinal disease omitted at cap.
Phenylalanine metabolism disorder; cognitive and developmental impairment are defining manifestations of the described symptomatic phenotype, preventable with treatment.
Recrudescent R. prowazekii infection targets vascular endothelium and causes small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash does not add a skin axis.
Mild legionellosis without pneumonia; cough, myalgia and headache do not establish pulmonary, muscle or neurologic damage.
Severe intellectual disability and structural CNS anomalies define the neurologic disease; acromegaly and abnormal growth-hormone physiology support the endocrine axis.
Inherited susceptibility to bipolar mood disorder; neurologic ancestry does not establish direct nervous-system damage.
Fibro-osseous replacement defines bone disease; phosphate-wasting hypophosphatemia is annotated frequent (30-79%); endocrine syndromes are not assumed.
Inherited erythrocyte glycolysis defect causes chronic hemolytic anemia; hemolytic jaundice does not establish liver injury; gallstones are a separate complication.
Congenital cafe-au-lait macules define the syndrome; developmental delay, cardiomyopathy and reflux are reported without established >=30% frequencies.
Embolic obstruction directly affects pulmonary arteries; lung infarction occurs in a minority and does not justify an additional pulmonary axis.
